summary: The fixed target leaves INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE disabled on both sides. That existing compile-time guard blocks the no-value handler before and after the change.

coverage_evidence.dependency_reason: Shows the fixed build recipe used on both sides.
Shows the fixed entry and sole parser call.

claims.necessity_reason: Necessity is established by the review. Timing compares the same no-value handler coverage obligation under the fixed old target.

before.requirement: Cover the supported no-value handler in the string-parser operation. The old source additionally bars its post-error variant with an !error guard.
before.reason: The old target does not enable INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE, so the handler path is compiled out even for an ordinary name-only line. The earlier-error state also fails the old !error guard.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Establishes that enabling the format was supported before the change.

after.requirement: Cover the changed no-value handler behavior when a name-only line follows an earlier parse error.
after.reason: The removed !error guard permits post-error handling, but the same target build still leaves INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE disabled.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Establishes the supported enabling option after the change.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Shows that the same string-parser call and input guard apply on both sides.

claims.comparison_reason: The innermost guard that prevents no-value handler execution under this build is the unchanged INI_ALLOW_NO_VALUE preprocessor condition. Removing the old !error guard extends behavior behind that already-unsatisfied condition.
